cards.b: Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day, moving roughly 5 litres of blood per minute at rest. Every cell needs oxygen and food delivered and waste removed. Heart disease is India's leading cause of death, so this one is useful to know.

Blood has red cells (carry oxygen using haemoglobin), white cells (defence), platelets (clotting) and plasma (liquid). Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure; veins bring it back, with valves; capillaries are thin walls where exchange happens.

The human heart has two atria (receive) and two ventricles (pump). The right side handles blood without oxygen; the left side handles blood with oxygen. Valves keep flow one-way, making the 'lub-dub' sound.

Blood passes through the heart twice per full round. The pulmonary circuit goes heart to lungs and back. The systemic circuit goes heart to body and back. This keeps oxygen-rich and poor blood apart and lets the body get high pressure. The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps to the whole body.

The heart has its own pacemaker, the sino-atrial (SA) node, which sends electrical signals across the atria, then through the AV node to the ventricles. An ECG records this. Blood pressure is written like 120/80 mmHg (systolic over diastolic). Nerves and hormones such as adrenaline change the rate.

Fat (cholesterol) deposits narrow arteries (atherosclerosis). A blocked coronary artery causes a heart attack. Blood clots are formed when platelets and fibrin seal a wound; vitamin K helps. High BP, smoking, diabetes and inactivity raise risk.

William Harvey (1628) showed that blood circulates, rather than being used up. Marcello Malpighi (1661) saw capillaries. Karl Landsteiner (1901) discovered ABO blood groups. Christiaan Barnard performed the first human heart transplant in 1967.

Fix these

  • Arteries do not always carry oxygen-rich blood; the pulmonary artery does not.
  • The heart is on the left only in feel; it sits mostly mid-chest.
  • Heart attack differs from cardiac arrest (electrical failure).

The first successful heart transplant in India was done by Dr P. Venugopal at AIIMS, Delhi, in 1994. Dr Devi Shetty pioneered low-cost cardiac surgery. The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases covers hypertension screening, and Indians show earlier heart disease than many populations.

• Heart: 4 chambers, double circulation.
  • Arteries away, veins back, capillaries exchange.
  • SA node is the pacemaker.
  • Atherosclerosis causes heart attacks.

Think about it:

  1. Why is the left ventricle wall thicker?
  2. Why are valves needed in veins but not in arteries?
